Thanks for sharing. Quick answers:

- Procurement needs a single invoice per quarter if possible; split invoicing is allowed but adds a 3-week processing delay. PO numbers will be provided once legal confirms the amendment.

A couple of asks from our side before we loop legal:
1) Can you show the net unit cost (USD per 1M tokens) for each scenario after discounting?
2) We need a short note on data handling (just a paragraph) so we can attach to the procurement packet.

If you can get the revised model and the data note by EOD Monday, I’ll aim to pull Procurement into the call next week.

David — forwarding Liam's answers and my suggested approach. Put bluntly: we have three levers to move (price, credit offset, commit term). Below is an internal pricing matrix I recommend you test in the model before sending back: 

- Conservative (no exec sign-off needed): +12% uplift, 0% extra discount, 3-month bridge to co-term, invoice per quarter; minimal credits.
- Balanced (requires AM sign-off): +25% uplift, one-time usage credit equal to 10% of uplift value, co-term immediate with amortized credit across first two invoices.
- Aggressive (exec approval required): +40% uplift, 20% volume discount for first year, pre-funded voucher equal to 15% of annual spend to smooth cash flow. Exec review if discount > 25%.

Notes: 
- Net unit cost (USD per 1M tokens) should be shown in the model for each scenario and include amortized credits.
- Procurement's single invoice preference argues for amortizing credits rather than issuing split invoices.
- If Finance demands split invoices, include a 1.5% processing fee to account for extra ops (we can absorb at the margin if needed).

Attaching: redwood-pricing-terms-v2.pdf (internal reference) and internal_approval_request.docx (form to route for >25% discounts).

If David can finalize the balanced option with net unit costs and a one-paragraph data handling note, we’ll prep a one-pager to send to Liam + Procurement.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
VP Sales — Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-pricing-terms-v2.pdf (PDF), internal_approval_request.docx (DOCX)
